description: Sir James Book003 - Chapters 1-5 Scene Cards for Parents Dashboard (Baseline → Skills)

book_structure.chapters_1_5: Foundation Skills (Baseline, Patterns, Teamwork, Communication, Transfer)
book_structure.chapters_6_10: Literacy Skills (Word Families, Blends, Sentences, Adjectives, Review)

opening.title: Sir James as Our Test Pilot
opening.setting: The Room of Many Windows - a round stone hall where glowing windows represent parent dashboard screens
opening.narrative: Sir James stands in a round stone hall called the Room of Many Windows, where each glowing window secretly represents a parent's dashboard screen in our world. Gramps explains that every time a grown-up taps a button, types in the chat box, or changes a slider, the windows shimmer and new adventures appear for Sir James, Claude, and Sparky to test.
opening.meta_purpose: Sir James is the first explorer of the Parents' Control Tower, testing each challenge so the Story Guides (A2A producer and director agents) can watch signals, adjust difficulty, and save what works into the Book of Measurements.

story_fields.setting: Little cottage on the edge of Whispering Woods, morning light, door to adventure

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James wakes in the little cottage on the edge of Whispering Woods, excited and a tiny bit nervous about his first 'official' quest, while Claude and Sparky bounce at the door.

child_challenge.prompt: Choose between a sunny path and a shadowy shortcut

a2a_hooks.measurement: survival-sense: Does child tend to rush, pause, or seek help?

choice_a.text: Let's take the safe sunny path!

choice_b.text: I'm brave enough for the shortcut!

story_fields.scene_title: Edge of the Woods, First Whisper Challenge
story_fields.setting: Forest edge where trees whisper soft clues about the safest way

scenes.narrative_beat: At the forest edge, the trees begin to 'whisper' soft clues about which way is safest, but they only make sense if Sir James slows down and listens carefully.

child_challenge.prompt: Listen to the forest whispers and choose which clue to follow

a2a_hooks.measurement: time spent + number of replays = attention span pattern

story_fields.setting: Deep in the trees, a friendly moss-covered Forest Guide offers help

scenes.narrative_beat: Deeper in the trees, Sir James meets a friendly, moss-covered Forest Guide who offers two kinds of help: a straight answer or a riddle.

child_challenge.prompt: Choose how the Forest Guide should help

parent_dashboard.chat_feature: Parent types wisdom that appears as 'grown-up wisdom' line in story margin

choice_b.text: Please help me find the way

story_fields.setting: Wind rattles branches, hollow log booms like a drum - sudden scare moment

scenes.narrative_beat: A sudden gust of wind rattles the branches and a hollow log booms like a drum, startling Sir James and Sparky, while Claude plants himself protectively at Sir James's side.

child_challenge.prompt: How are you feeling right now?

buttons.label: Practice Breathing
buttons.action: mini breathing exercise with Claude counting

parent_dashboard.display: Child's emoji selection visible to parent

a2a_hooks.producer_signal: emotional_regulation preference (push ahead vs linger and calm)

choice_a.text: I feel scared but I'll keep going!

choice_b.text: Let's take a breath with Claude

story_fields.setting: Small camp just inside the safe ring of trees, evening falls

scenes.narrative_beat: As evening falls, they make a small camp just inside the safe ring of trees, and Sir James, Gramps, Claude, and Sparky talk about what went well and what still feels tricky.

child_challenge.prompt: Choose one moment each of:
child_challenge.display: Icons light up above the scene

parent_dashboard.display: Summary Card: 'Today your child: listened to forest clues, chose X path, used Y hints, told us they felt Z'

a2a_hooks.director_agent: adjusts Chapter 2 difficulty and hint density based on parent clicks

foreshadow.hint: Tomorrow we enter the Crystal Caves where patterns glow!

story_fields.setting: Mouth of Crystal Caves - thousands of colored crystals hum softly, doorway shifts shape

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James reaches the mouth of the Crystal Caves, where thousands of colored crystals hum softly like a choir, and the doorway itself shifts shape depending on how closely he looks.

child_challenge.prompt: Spot the pattern in the crystals to open the door

a2a_hooks.measurement: thinking-survival profile (no red X's, just patterns)

story_fields.setting: Chamber where every question echoes back with a slightly different version

scenes.narrative_beat: Inside, Sir James finds a chamber where every question he asks echoes back with a slightly different version, teaching him that good questions help light up the cave.

child_challenge.prompt: Help Sir James ask a good question
child_challenge.skill_measured: metacognition - learning that questions are survival skills

parent_dashboard.action: Parent choice triggers narrator to pose that style of question

a2a_hooks.measurement: metacognition training: 'What do I notice?' as survival skill

story_fields.setting: Glowing chasm with stepping-stone path, Claude's nose glows as he sniffs safe path

scenes.narrative_beat: Claude pads ahead, his nose glowing faintly as he sniffs out a safe stepping-stone path across a glowing chasm, while Sparky races along a ledge above.

child_challenge.prompt: Choose the crystal sequence to cross safely

a2a_hooks.d2a_signal: D2A documentation agent logs help needed
a2a_hooks.director_note: Future chapters present near-but-not-quite-familiar puzzles instead of random difficulty jumps

story_fields.setting: Unusually dark and quiet section of cave

scenes.narrative_beat: A section of the cave grows unusually dark and quiet, and Sir James admits that even brave knights can feel unsure when they can't see the way.

child_challenge.prompt: How should Sir James feel better?

silly_song.label: Sing a silly song with Sparky

parent_dashboard.purpose: Soft emotional map for fun-scary vs too-much correlation

story_fields.setting: Chapter end - floating crystal ledger appears with badges

scenes.narrative_beat: At the chapter's end, a floating crystal ledger appears, showing icons for patterns solved, questions tried, hints used, and coping choices, all in a playful badge-like style.

child_challenge.display: Badge icons: patterns solved, questions tried, hints used, coping choices

suggestions: Next time: try fewer automatic hints
Offer more 'ask a question' prompts via chat

foreshadow.hint: The Labyrinth awaits, where teamwork lights the way!

choice_a.text: I learned to ask good questions!

choice_b.text: I tried hard even when stuck!

story_fields.setting: Huge stone map of labyrinth that rearranges when touched

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James, Gramps, Claude, and Sparky stand before a huge stone map of a labyrinth that rearranges itself when they touch it, representing all the upcoming choices.

child_challenge.prompt: Help Sir James pick a route

parent_dashboard.note: This choice shapes how many mini-challenges we show today

story_fields.setting: Inside the maze - gates respond to different characters' strengths

scenes.narrative_beat: Inside the maze, the group must get through a series of gates that each respond best to a different character—Claude's nose, Sparky's agility, Gramps's wisdom, or Sir James's courage.

child_challenge.prompt: Who should try first? Who should lead this time?

parent_dashboard.display: Character selection counter - which character child picks most often

story_fields.setting: Twisting corridor filled with silver mist, Labyrinth Guardian appears as faint outline

scenes.narrative_beat: A twisting corridor fills with silver mist that makes it hard to see, but the Labyrinth Guardian appears as a faint outline to offer a choice: rush ahead following a faint light, or pause to draw a plan in the dust.

child_challenge.prompt: Should Sir James plan first or jump into action?

plan.label: Draw a plan in the dust

story_fields.setting: Tricky gap with shifting stepping stone

scenes.narrative_beat: At one tricky gap, a stepping stone shifts under Sir James's foot, and he has to decide whether to leap alone or grab Claude's collar and trust him to guide the jump.

child_challenge.prompt: Leap alone or trust Claude?

parent_dashboard.prompt: Ask your child what they would do if they were Sir James

a2a_hooks.d2a_signal: family_discussion flag enables similar reflection prompts later

story_fields.scene_title: Bridge of Light Finale & Virtue Wrap-Up
story_fields.setting: Radiant Bridge of Light appears from combined decisions

scenes.narrative_beat: Finally, the group reaches the radiant Bridge of Light, where all the day's quiet decisions combine to let the bridge appear beneath Sir James's feet. The Guardian formally names the three key virtues: courage, wisdom, and trust.

child_challenge.prompt: Which virtue felt strongest for you? Which would you like to practice more?

parent_dashboard.display: Mini-graph of virtue choices across Chapters 1-3

a2a_hooks.director_agent: clear knobs for shaping Chapter 4 and beyond

foreshadow.hint: Next: Skyward Harbor where words take flight!

story_fields.setting: Floating harbor where airships drift among clouds, dockmasters give conflicting directions

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James sails to a floating harbor where airships drift among clouds, and every dockmaster seems to give slightly different instructions.

child_challenge.prompt: How should Sir James handle the confusing directions?

toggle.label: Practice Asking for Clarity
toggle.description: When on, narrator and NPCs reward question-asking more heavily

choice_a.text: Can you say that again please?

story_fields.setting: Humorous misunderstanding about which ship to board

scenes.narrative_beat: Claude mishears an instruction and Sparky over-explains something, leading to a humorous misunderstanding about which ship they're boarding.

child_challenge.prompt: Help Sir James say it better

parent_dashboard.display: Tone palette - shows child's usual tone picks (direct/friendly/goofy)

chat_box.prompt: Type a real-life example from your family
chat_box.example: We had a mix-up at school pickup this week

a2a_hooks.d2a_signal: Parent context stored for future story mirroring (no personal details exposed)

choice_a.text: Let me be clear: which ship?

story_fields.setting: High tower with colorful flags that change shape based on listening quality

scenes.narrative_beat: High above the harbor, colorful flags change shape depending on how well characters listen to one another. Sir James must listen to a sky-captain's story and choose what mattered most.

child_challenge.prompt: What mattered most in the captain's story?

story_fields.setting: Dark clouds gather, harbor goes on alert with sirens and flapping sails

scenes.narrative_beat: Dark clouds gather and the harbor goes on alert, with sirens and flapping sails making the scene noisy and busy. Sir James has to calm Sparky, follow instructions, and notice a crucial clue Claude finds.

child_challenge.prompt: How should Sir James stay calm and lead?

button.label: Use Calm-Leader Script
button.description: Story models what calm leadership sounds like

a2a_hooks.producer_signal: calming_tactic_preference promoted as reusable survival pattern

choice_a.text: Deep breath... we can do this!

story_fields.setting: Storm passes, harbor master thanks the team

scenes.narrative_beat: When the storm passes, the harbor master thanks Sir James and friends, and invites them to hang a small flag that represents how they handled the day.

child_challenge.prompt: What should your flag mean?

parent_dashboard.chat_prompt: What's a time your family stayed calm together?

a2a_hooks.d2a_signal: Bookmarked scenes feed D2A documentation pipeline for 'great moments to revisit'

foreshadow.hint: The Clockwork Library holds all our memories!

story_fields.setting: Library where shelves glide on rails, each book is a mechanical box replaying past adventures

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James steps into a library where shelves glide on rails and each book is a small mechanical box that replays a past adventure as tiny holograms.

child_challenge.prompt: Which adventure memory box do you want to open?

parent_dashboard.description: Direct control over which type of mini-activity appears beneath the recap

choice_b.text: Let's see how we solved puzzles!

story_fields.scene_title: Claude's Code Room (APIs in Story Form)
story_fields.setting: Cozy room full of glowing runes and sliding tiles representing 'promises between worlds'

scenes.narrative_beat: Claude leads Sir James to a cozy room full of glowing runes and sliding tiles where each tile represents a 'promise' between worlds: when a child does X, the system does Y. Gramps explains this is how adventures know when to change.

child_challenge.prompt: Arrange the tiles to make promises

overlay.description: Maps tiles to trigger types (hint requests, virtue selections, parent chat events)

parent_dashboard.purpose: Gives designers and engineers a narrative-safe way to think about sequential API calls

a2a_hooks.meta_purpose: Metaphor for actual APIs programming team is building

choice_b.text: If I help friends, they help me!

story_fields.setting: Carved wooden desk labeled 'For Grown-Up Co-Adventurers Only' with blank pages

scenes.narrative_beat: Sir James discovers a carved wooden desk labeled 'For Grown-Up Co-Adventurers Only,' where blank pages wait for new challenges.

child_challenge.prompt: What kind of challenge should the grown-ups create?
child_challenge.display: Child sees that parents can add to their adventures

panel.title: Parent Authoring Panel
panel.input: Add a simple prompt or family detail

a2a_hooks.producer_agent: Turns parent choices into safe, on-rails micro-variations
a2a_hooks.d2a_agent: Tracks which templates families actually use for cost-effectiveness

story_fields.setting: Friendly clockwork owl with spinning dials showing growth icons

scenes.narrative_beat: Near the exit stands a friendly clockwork owl that spins dials labeled with icons rather than numbers: a growing tree for persistence, a rising sun for confidence, interlocking gears for teamwork, and a glowing ear for listening.

examples: Your teamwork tree grew new leaves!

details: Which chapters contributed most to which skills
How often reflection questions were used

parent_dashboard.description: This is your Book of Measurements - aggregated but playful

a2a_hooks.purpose: Informs agents about where to stretch or support in upcoming books

story_fields.setting: Labyrinth Guardian shows five distant landmarks - mountains, rivers, towers

scenes.narrative_beat: As Sir James leaves the Clockwork Library, the Labyrinth Guardian appears one last time to show him five distant landmarks—mountains, rivers, towers—that hint at the next five chapters still to come.

child_challenge.prompt: What kind of place should we visit next?

parent_dashboard.purpose: Tags family preference, gives programming team clear routing for APIs

a2a_hooks.director_agent: Proposes which upcoming adventures best match child's emerging strengths and struggles

foreshadow.destination: Chapters 6-10: River of Choices, Echo Mountain, City of Many Doors, Star Orchard, Homecoming Circle

scenes.closing: And so Sir James looked toward the horizon, ready for new adventures. The Room of Many Windows glowed warmly, as parents everywhere prepared to guide the next journey... For the Commons Good! 🏰⚔️🐕✨

book_of_measurements.description: Aggregated skill tracking without grades, just patterns

tracked_skills.survival_sense: Does child rush, pause, or seek help?
tracked_skills.transfer_survival: Ability to connect skills across chapters

virtue_tracking.display: Icons that light up, no numbers/grades for children

parent_view.recommendations: A2A agent suggestions for next sessions

api_flow_summary.chapter_5: Transfer practice → comprehensive skill gauge + Chapters 6-10 seeding
